World’s largest balloon constellation

# Atlas

Our global sensing constellation delivers the critical observations that are closing the atmospheric data gap.

![Multiple WindBorne Global Sounding Balloons ascending through a blue sky](https://windbornesystems.com/_astro/hero-multi-launch.Db7I9A31_ZEPVda.webp)

## The atmospheric data gap

### The problem and our solution

Weather regularly blows in from unpopulated areas—but these areas are critically under-observed. For example, when hurricanes form in the Atlantic, humanity can't measure them with radiosondes or other ground-based technologies that form the backbone of the weather network on land. The resulting weather uncertainty costs tens of billions every year in the U.S. alone and results in loss of life worldwide.

To close the atmospheric data gap worldwide, WindBorne operates and maintains **Atlas**—a global sensing network that comprises the largest balloon constellation in the world, continuously collecting in-situ atmospheric soundings. It operates pole to pole, including those remote areas where key weather systems form. Atlas is powered by autonomous, long-duration high-altitude balloons called **Global Sounding Balloons (GSBs)** that drastically improve upon legacy weather balloons in performance, endurance, sustainability, and cost. Atlas currently maintains hundreds of GSBs aloft globally.

At scale, Atlas will encompass the globe with 10,000 GSBs concurrently aloft—the coverage level cited by the World Meteorological Organization as adequate for weather forecasting.

[View API docs](https://api.windbornesystems.com/) [Access WindBorne Live](https://windbornesystems.com/live)

Persistent global coverage

## Building a planetary nervous system

Atlas is the only balloon network capable of providing consistent, comprehensive atmospheric coverage worldwide.

- ### Global launch network



A launch network spanning six continents supports persistent worldwide coverage.

- ### Vast data collection



Atlas collects millions of kilometers of atmospheric observations every month.

- ### Autonomous navigation



Our flight system uses wind patterns to guide balloons toward high-value target regions, maximizing coverage where it matters most.

- ### Rapid deployment



WindBorne’s lean launch operations let a single operator launch multiple GSBs per day, so coverage scales fast.


## From the surface to the stratosphere

![WindBorne Live dashboard showing observations from a balloon over the northwest Pacific Ocean](https://windbornesystems.com/_astro/live-dashboard.DlxqJOnM_1Snope.webp)

Data as a service

### Continuous profiles across remote regions

Coverage where you need it

Continuous global coverage, with the ability to surge coverage toward specific regions or weather events.

Delivered in near real-time

Observations are available within about 10 minutes of collection via API and WindBorne Live. Data is also shared with forecasters worldwide through the WMO Global Telecommunication System.

Trusted scientific standards

Distributed via the WMO GTS and assimilated into NOAA’s Global Forecast System. NOAA studies have confirmed that WindBorne observations improve forecast accuracy.

Forecast impact

### Better inputs make better forecasts

Weather models depend on atmospheric observations. Augmenting current data collections can lead to significantly [more accurate forecasts](https://windbornesystems.com/platform/forecasts), and closing the atmospheric data gap can ensure a future in which weather certainty becomes a reality. WindBorne data is distributed globally through the WMO Global Telecommunication System and assimilated into [NOAA’s Global Forecast System](https://wpo.noaa.gov/windborne-weather-balloon-reaches-new-heights/).

NOAA studies have shown that WindBorne observations improve the accuracy of physics-based forecast models.

![Temperature and wind forecast map over North America with WindBorne balloon locations](https://windbornesystems.com/_astro/forecast-impact.ShvZdic__5UN6l.webp)

How Atlas works

## Built to stay aloft and keep collecting

Our proprietary balloon technology allows us to collect critical [atmospheric data](https://api.windbornesystems.com/models-measurements/measurements/in-situ-data/) worldwide.

Payload weight**<1.3kg** less than 2.8 lb

Real-time data**10min** on average, from collection to user delivery

Typical flight**15+days** with a record flight of 345 days

- 01


### Precision altitude control



Each flight collects dozens of vertical profiles from surface to stratosphere.

- 02


### Advanced navigation



Wind-aware routing guides balloons toward target locations.

- 03


### Proven performance



Demonstrated capability for multiple [circumnavigations](https://windbornesystems.com/blog/flight-w-2162-the-odyssey-of-a-windborne-global-sounding-balloon) and global coverage.

- 04


### Solar-powered sensors



Each GSB measures temperature, humidity, pressure, and wind.

- 05


### Satellite communications



Observations transmitted in near real-time to our customers and forecasting systems worldwide.

- 06


### Active Plane Avoidance



Onboard [ADS-B](https://windbornesystems.com/faq#airplanes) detects nearby aircraft, with avoidance that works even without a satellite link.


1. ### GSB-deployed dropsondes




Atlas can deploy lightweight atmospheric sensors into severe storms from balloons already in flight, multiplying data collection without additional launches. Unlike traditional aircraft-deployed dropsondes, this eliminates aircraft and pilot risk. WindBorne has successfully deployed sensors [directly into hurricanes](https://windbornesystems.com/blog/how-windborne-navigated-first-ever-balloon-deployed-dropsondes-directly-into-hurricane-milton).

2. ### GSB-to-buoy capability




GSBs feature the world’s first [balloon-to-buoy](https://spectrum.ieee.org/ai-weather-forecasting-balloons-buoys) capability. After completing atmospheric data collection, GSBs transition into buoys, detaching their envelopes in order to continue operating as ocean buoys and extending coverage across both atmospheric and marine domains.


![Illustration of a balloon deploying a dropsonde into a hurricane above a coastline](https://windbornesystems.com/_astro/expansion-dropsonde-cloud.wJJYi6Oo_Z2j9s6F.webp)![Illustration of an ocean buoy transmitting observations to balloons overhead](https://windbornesystems.com/_astro/expansion-buoy-cloud.Da0vr9fx_Z2aH5mp.webp)
